summary: Silver nanoparticles (nanosilver) are an engineered silver-based broad-spectrum antimicrobial used chiefly in wound dressings, coatings and antiseptic preparations. Silver ions released from the particles damage microbial membranes, proteins and DNA, giving activity against bacteria (including some resistant strains), fungi and biofilm. There is no established systemic/oral therapeutic dose; use is topical and product-specific. Chronic or systemic silver exposure can cause argyria (irreversible grey discoloration). Nanosilver is not FDA-approved as a systemic drug; many products are regulated as medical devices or are unapproved supplements.

moa: Silver nanoparticles release silver ions (Ag+) and, by virtue of their high surface area, exert antimicrobial effects through multiple mechanisms: disruption of microbial cell membranes and the respiratory chain, binding to thiol groups of essential enzymes, generation of reactive oxygen species, and interaction with microbial DNA - inhibiting replication. This broad, multi-target action limits resistance development.

absolute: Ingestion / systemic use (no approved systemic indication)
relative: Application over extensive burns or denuded skin (systemic absorption)
Use with topical enzymatic debriding agents that silver may inactivate

Serum silver levels only if extensive/prolonged exposure suspected

preg: Avoid systemic or oral silver exposure in pregnancy; topical use over small areas is generally regarded as low risk but data are limited - use only if necessary.
lact: Avoid oral/systemic silver while breastfeeding; limited data exist for topical use over small areas.
renal: No oral therapeutic indication; with extensive topical exposure silver may accumulate, so caution is advised in renal impairment. There is no established dose adjustment.
hepatic: No oral therapeutic indication; silver is partly handled by the liver, so avoid significant systemic exposure in hepatic impairment.

missed: Not applicable as a fixed dose schedule; topical dressings are simply changed at the next scheduled time per the product instructions if a change is missed.
overdose: Acute topical overdose is unlikely. Excessive or systemic silver exposure (especially ingestion) can cause argyria and, rarely, organ toxicity. There is no specific antidote; manage by stopping exposure and providing supportive care.
